A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MemTree paper, with 34 complete pages including Appendices A–C. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results in Tables 1–4, supplementary experiments in Appendix A.3, and a human evaluation in Appendix A.3.8.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark, ablation, and human-evaluation results. Their retention from v2 does not change their status as original empirical results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A.1 retain the same tree insertion, depth-adaptive threshold, content aggregation, and collapsed-tree retrieval procedures. Algorithm 1 is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MSC, MSC-E, QuALITY, and MultiHop RAG with the same conversational and document-question-answering coverage. The human-evaluation task and supplementary test scenarios are also retained unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments: full-context baselines, MemoryStream, MemGPT, RAPTOR, GraphRAG, and human-annotated evidence retain their respective roles in Tables 1–4. Appendix comparisons are unchanged.

E3.justification: The versions specify identical models, sample sizes, chunking, retrieval limits, context lengths, and evaluation metrics. The appendix protocols, including the 500-question study with five annotators, are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 retains the same evidence-position analysis, retrieval and model ablations, threshold sensitivity, human evaluation, efficiency analysis, and prompt-compression experiments. Appendix C retains the same retrieval examples and failure cases.

E5.justification: The same uncertainty bands, error bars, variability statistics, and statistical-significance statements appear in both versions, including Figure A.1 and Appendices A.3.7–A.3.8. No run-count, seed, or uncertainty-estimation information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical and qualitative results are unchanged throughout. For example, MemTree's overall accuracy remains 82.5% on MSC-E, 59.8% on QuALITY, and 80.5% on MultiHop RAG in Tables 2–4. Appendix results and failure examples also match.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and Appendix B retain the same approximation guarantee, Moseley-Wang revenue definition, beta-well-separated assumption, and depth-adaptive-threshold derivation. No mathematical argument is added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion make the same claims about dynamic hierarchical memory, efficient online updates, and performance across four benchmarks. The publication-status update does not alter the scientific contribution claims.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same interpretations of recency bias, hierarchical organization, efficiency tradeoffs, and robustness. Appendix C's explanations of failures caused by buried or insufficient evidence are unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A.1–A.2 provide identical implementation settings, prompts, and data-generation instructions. Existing links and the reproducibility statement promising code release upon acceptance remain unchanged; v3 adds no access information.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including comparisons with memory-augmented LLMs, structured RAG, and online hierarchical clustering. No references or substantive prior-work distinctions are added or removed.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Preprint' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025', and the arXiv stamp updates the version and date. The body wording, terminology, section order, and appendix structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: There are cosmetic changes to header typography and the first-page arXiv stamp, plus an approximately 0.8-point vertical shift in some page-2 text. Figures, tables, captions, axes, legends, and their placement are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 updates publication metadata and makes negligible typographic adjustments while retaining the same scientific content across the main text and appendices. The method, empirical evidence, theoretical arguments, interpretations, and reproducibility information are unchanged, so there is no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
